note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

emerging_candidates.how_to_use: RAW watchlist of non-radar chains rising on the signals below — NOT buy calls. A candidate becomes a LEAD only on confluence (also trending / in a heating narrative / has a catalyst / fresh dev-gov) or a confirmed on-chain TVL surge.

signal_glossary.volume_heat: Volume is large vs market cap (turnover ≥15%) — unusual interest building.
signal_glossary.vol_leads_price: Volume is hot but 7d price hasn't run yet — interest building BEFORE the move (the early sweet spot).
signal_glossary.momentum: 7d gain keeping pace with / exceeding 30d — the move is accelerating, not fading.
signal_glossary.low_float: Only a small share of supply circulates — CAUTION: unlock overhang can cap upside.
signal_glossary.tvl_surge: On-chain TVL jumped ≥25% in 7d from a small base — real capital arriving, not just token price.

pre_winner_lookalikes.method: validated winner-DNA coil screen (deep-below-high + oversold + at-30d-low [all validated, hold OOS] + below-ATH/high-vol/mid-float/small-cap); primed-but-not-yet-moved. NECESSARY-not-sufficient setup — needs an event trigger.
pre_winner_lookalikes.how_to_use: Beaten-down coils matching the data-validated winner DNA. SETUPS, not buys: most never move. Edge comes ONLY from confluence — a lookalike that is also trending / in a heating narrative / has a near catalyst / has fresh dev-gov.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

## Protocol
#### Sui Protocol Version in this release: `137`

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27844: Ristretto255 range proof verification is cheaper and the limit on the number of commitments times the range bit length is raised from 512 to 1024, so larger batches can now be verified in a single call.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27528: adds `allowances` feature

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27524: Protocol v137 enables `check_object_funds_withdraw_in_execution` on devnet only. Object-funds withdrawal sufficiency is checked inside the Move VM at the point of withdrawal, insufficient withdrawals abort with a `sui::funds_accumulator` Move abort, and the first settled-balance read for each `(owner, type)` pair costs 184 internal gas units.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27930: In protocol version 137, `LdConst` charges gas for the abstract value size of the constant rather than its serialized byte length, slightly increasing gas costs for constant-heavy code.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27939: `TransactionExpiration::Validity` is now accepted on all networks, allowing a transaction to restrict which validators may propose it in consensus.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27938: Enables additional signing time checks to reject structurally invalid txs earlier.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27984: Adds new memory invariant check for reference/value usage in PTBs.

governance.title: Rotate Sentinel Addresses on the DUNI-Owned Uniswap Earn Vaults
governance.body:
## **TL;DR**

* DUNI owns the three Gauntlet-curated Morpho Vaults V2 behind Uniswap Earn: uniUSDC, uniUSDT and uniETH, all on Ethereum mainnet.   
* Gauntlet has upgraded its signing infrastructure and needs to swap out some wallets configured in the Sentinel role on vault deployment.  
* `setIsSentinel`, the function used to adjust addresses granted the Sentinel role, is owner-gated and the Owner is Uniswap governance’s mainnet Timelock.

## **Background**

Uniswap Labs launched Uniswap Earn in July 2026. Consistent with past Uniswap Labs-originated protocol launches, the ownership roles on the smart contracts that power Uniswap Earn were assigned to Uniswap Governance. In Earn, a user deposits USDC, USDT or ETH in the Uniswap app, the deposit flows into a Morpho Vaults V2 instance, and Gauntlet curates the allocation. In the run up to launch, Gauntlet deployed the three vaults and transferred ownership to DUNI’s Timelock address.

Morpho Vaults V2 splits control across four roles.

| Role | Capabilities | Appointed by | Held on the Earn vaults by |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Owner | Appoint the Curator, add and remove Sentinels, transfer ownership, set vault name and …[truncated]

governance.body:
*This proposal is part of the protocol fee rollout, following proposals [#93](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/93), [#94](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/94), [#95](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/95), [#96](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/96), [#99](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/99), and [#100](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/100). It uses the expedited governance process [approved](https://gov.uniswap.org/t/unification-proposal/25881#p-57882-protocol-fee-rollout-4) in UNIfication, where fee parameter update proposals can bypass the RFC stage and go directly to a five-day Snapshot followed by an onchain vote.*

Since protocol fees went live on Ethereum mainnet in late December last year, the rollout has extended to eleven additional chains: Arbitrum, Base, OP Mainnet, Worldchain, X Layer, Soneium, Zora, Celo, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Robinhood Chain. The burn system is working as designed, with fees accumulating in TokenJars across chains. From there, searchers claim them in exchange for burning UNI by bridging it back to mainnet and sending it to the burn address.

governance.title: Authorize a Contingent LDO CEX Liquidity Market-Making Mandate
governance.body:
### Summary

This proposal requests Lido DAO to authorize a contingent, capped market-making mandate for LDO on centralized exchanges (CEXs), to reduce the risk of LDO trading-pair degradation or delisting due to insufficient liquidity.

The authorization covers two funding caps from the Lido DAO Treasury, in addition to the approved EGG budget ([EGG-2026](https://research.lido.fi/t/ecosystem-grants-grequest-egg-a-budget-request-framework-in-the-service-of-goose/6053)).

- Up to the lower of $1,500,000 in LDO equivalent or 7,500,000 LDO, as a recallable facility for market-making inventory.
- Up to 480,000 USDC for fixed market-maker retainers and directly related costs; to be disbursed at the start of each quarter via Easy Track.

No funds may be drawn unless [the Lido Growth Committee](https://research.lido.fi/t/rationalizing-liquidity-observation-lab-rewards-share-committee-growth-committee/10133) determines that LDO liquidity on certain centralized exchanges is insufficient, or likely to become insufficient. ### TL;DR

This vote seeks Lido DAO approval for the appointment of [Leeward Supervisors Limited ("Leeward")](https://leeward.ky) as Supervisor of [Lido Alliance BORG Foundation ("Lido Alliance BORG")](https://research.lido.fi/t/organize-the-lido-alliance-program-as-a-lido-dao-adjacent-borg/8173).

Leeward is a Cayman Islands governance, compliance and fiduciary services firm specialising in Web3 and digital assets, and the current Supervisor of Lido Labs Foundation. Through that role, it is already familiar with the structure and functions of the entities operating adjacent to Lido DAO.

### Background

Lido Alliance BORG is a Cayman Islands foundation company established to support the purposes assigned to it under its governing documents as approved by Lido DAO. It has no members or beneficiaries, and its business and affairs are managed by or under the control of its board of directors. It is funded through [the Ecosystem Grant gRequest (EGG)](https://research.lido.fi/t/2026-ecosystem-grant-grequest-egg-executing-goose-3/10951).
